knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a Logarithmic Function With a General Base

question.:question/problem:
Given the function  $y=3{log}_{6}⁡x-5\operatorname{ln}⁡x+8{e}^{x},$ find the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1.$ Do not round the answer.

The instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is
{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To differentiate a logarithm with base $a,$ we use the formula

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({log}_{a}⁡x)=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡a}.
$$

To find the instantaneous rate of change at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Taking the derivative we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(3{log}_{6}⁡x-5\operatorname{ln}⁡x+8{e}^{x}) \\  & =\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡6}-\frac{5}{x}+8{e}^{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the instantaneous rate of change at $x=1$ is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=1} & ={(\frac{3}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡6}-\frac{5}{x}+8{e}^{x})\,|}_{x=1} \\  & =\frac{3}{1\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡6}-\frac{5}{1}+8{e}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{\operatorname{ln}⁡6}-5+8e\,.\end{aligned}
$$
